result.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import_remote calling `open(url).read` (topic_embed.rb) before any URL validation, and lib/tasks/disqus.thor passes t[:link] from an imported Disqus XML directly into import_remote (TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])). Ruby's Kernel#open executes shell commands for strings beginning with '|', so a malicious export file yields code execution during import. The `^https?://` check in `import` runs only after the open() call, so it does not mitigate this. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security vulnerability. Looking at the diff: 1) `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` shows `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` where `t[:link]` comes from parsed Disqus XML without validation. 2) `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` shows `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read,` which uses Ruby's `Kernel#open`. 3) Ruby's `open` with a string starting with `|` executes it as a shell command. 4) The URL validation `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` is in `import` method (line 10), but `import_remote` calls `open(url)` at line 48 BEFORE calling `import` at line 52. This means a malicious Disqus export with a `<link>` like `|malicious_command` would execute the command before any URL validation occurs. This is a legitimate command injection vulnerability.
